description: Wave Multiplier mixes four shifted copies of the input wave with the original, each copy shifted against its own threshold, with four triangle LFOs built in to modulate them

params.text: Sets the base frequency of all four LFOs on a volt per octave scale where 0 gives 1Hz; the range runs -4 to 4, and the default of -4 gives 0.0625Hz
Offsets that LFO's frequency from the base by as much as a volt either way; the four defaults are uncorrelated and spread over a little more than 1.5 octaves
Sets how far the wave copies are shifted, 0V to 5V, with the attenuated CV added on top
Attenuates or inverts the depth CV
Attenuates or inverts that copy's shift threshold CV
Sets the base shift threshold for that copy, -5V to 5V, with the attenuated CV added on top; input above the threshold is shifted down, input at or below it is shifted up
Removes DC offset from the pulse, shifted wave and mix outputs; on by default
Sets oversampling against the aliasing shifting and audio rate level modulation introduce: off, x2, x4 by default, x8, x16 or x32
Takes that shifted wave out of the final mix
Takes the raw input wave out of the final mix
Attenuates or inverts the output level CV
Sets the base level of the mix output, 0 to 100% with a default of 25%, with the attenuated CV summed on top

inputs.text: Summed with the master frequency to set the base frequency of all four LFOs
Voltage control of the shift depth, attenuated and summed with the Depth knob; audio rate CV works
Modulates that copy's shift threshold; unpatched it follows the matching LFO output. Audio rate CV works
The wave to be multiplied, typically audio; sine, triangle and saw suit it, square and pulse do not
Voltage control of the mix level, 10V for 100%; negative voltage inverts the output, so the level stage can work as a ring modulator. Audio rate CV works

outputs.text: A bipolar triangle LFO at 5V either way, normalled to the shift threshold CV input of the matching copy
The bipolar 5V pulse from that copy's comparator, with the depth not applied; modulating the threshold gives pulse width modulation here
That copy's pulse attenuated by the depth and summed with the input wave
The mix of the unmuted shifted waves and the unmuted input wave, scaled by the output level

notes: the LFOs run monophonic unless the master V/OCT input is polyphonic, in which case they take the channel count of the rest of the module
menu: Oversample filter quality — 10th order by default, with 8th order and a cheaper 6th order; 10th and 8th cut at 80% of Nyquist and 6th at 50%
